description: Use AVX-512 gather/scatter instructions to implement a 'token router' that reads tokens from scattered input positions and writes parsed results to scattered output positions in a single vectorized operation. Eliminates the sequential pointer-chasing of one-at-a-time structural index traversal by processing 8-16 entries in parallel.
mathematical_formalization: Structural index entries P[0..15]. VPGATHERDQ loads 8-byte values at each position: V[i] = input[P[i]..P[i]+7]. Classify in parallel: class[i] = lookup[V[i][0]]. VPSCATTERDQ stores results. Total: 3 instructions for 16 tokens vs. ~80 scalar instructions. Speedup: ~26x for token classification.
analogical_connections: Network packet routing: packets arrive/depart at scattered ports
Vectorized database execution (MonetDB/X100): process column batches through vectorized primitives
Ko et al. speculative DFA: SIMD gather for indexed memory loads in vectorized DFA matching
implementation_hypothesis: Load 16 structural index entries into zmm. VPGATHERDQ loads first 8 bytes at each position. Classify via VPSHUFB on first byte. For number/boolean/null tokens, attempt SIMD inline parsing. For strings, record start positions. Scatter results to columnar output. Process in batches of 16.
experiment_seed: Benchmark gather-scatter token router vs. sequential traversal. Measure tokens/second, gather latency vs. sequential loads, efficiency on different JSON shapes. Test on 1M-integer JSON array. Target: >2x throughput for value-dense JSON.
